message.content: We're rolling out the new payments service next week. Should we use staging-only feature flags like we did for the auth flow?

The staging-only flag policy worked for the auth flow because rollout failures could be contained — auth failures degraded to 'user has to retry login', and staging traffic was representative enough to surface bugs. The reversibility was load-bearing for that choice.

Payments mutate external state via Stripe — a charge that goes through can't just be 'undeployed'. Refund flow exists but is its own service surface that can fail. So staging-only doesn't actually contain blast radius the way it did for auth: even successful staging tests don't tell you what production will do, because staging Stripe is sandbox-mode and behaves differently from live.
So we need a different gating strategy?

Right. Options: (1) shadow-mode in production where the new service runs but doesn't issue real charges; (2) percentage rollout on a small cohort (say 1%) with full monitoring; (3) route-by-merchant where opt-in merchants take the new path. Each has tradeoffs but all preserve a real-state-mutation feedback loop that staging can't replicate.
Shadow mode plus a 1% cohort sounds right. Let's ship the policy.

Will document the payments-specific gating policy. Key reframe: 'staging-only' was a property of the auth flow's reversibility, not a universal best practice. Different services need flag policies tied to their failure mode.
Good. Let's also note this in the broader feature-flag policy doc so future services don't inherit the staging-only assumption.
